title: Customer Segments by Spending Quartile
description: Segment customers into **4 spending tiers** based on their total purchase amount using `NTILE(4)`. Label them: Q1='Low Spender', Q2='Mid Spender', Q3='High Spender', Q4='Top Spender'. Show each customer's total_spent, quartile number, and segment label.
solution_sql: WITH customer_spending AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id), segmented AS (SELECT customer_id, total_spent, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_spent) AS spending_quartile FROM customer_spending) SELECT customer_id, total_spent, spending_quartile, CASE spending_quartile WHEN 1 THEN 'Low Spender' WHEN 2 THEN 'Mid Spender' WHEN 3 THEN 'High Spender' ELSE 'Top Spender' END AS segment FROM segmented ORDER BY total_spent DESC

test_cases.description: 8 customers in 4 quartiles of 2 each. Sorted: C6=6500, C2=3500, C4=1800, C8=1600, C1=1000, C7=550, C3=250, C5=125.

hints: First aggregate total spending per customer in a CTE, then apply NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_spent) in a second CTE to divide customers into 4 equal-sized quartile groups.
NTILE(4) assigns values 1-4 — use CASE to map 1→'Low Spender', 2→'Mid Spender', 3→'High Spender', 4→'Top Spender'.
explanation: NTILE(4) divides 8 customers into 4 groups of 2. Sorted ascending by total_spent: C5(125)=Q1, C3(250)=Q1 → 'Low Spender'. C7(550)=Q2, C1(1000)=Q2 → 'Mid Spender'. C8(1600)=Q3, C4(1800)=Q3 → 'High Spender'. C2(3500)=Q4, C6(6500)=Q4 → 'Top Spender'. This segmentation drives targeted marketing: discounts for low spenders, loyalty programs for top spenders.
